messages:
support_andy: Hey #incidents — ACME (high-usage tenant) reporting intermittent 503s and stalled streaming responses for long-context requests since ~09:12 UTC. Impacting p95/p99, several customers seeing timeouts. Raising here for triage.
oncall-bot: [alert] hosted-infer upstream error rate spike: 503s (service: upstream-runner). Alerting oncall.
alex_w: acked, pinging eng-runtime. Any obvious recent deploys or model swaps around 09:00?
maria_g: we rolled a hotmodel swap to v2-quant at 08:58 for capacity. I have a hunch long-context + quantized runtime might be growing KV cache unexpectedly.
jamal: I can repro locally with a long stream. Steps: curl -N -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"v2-quant","prompt":"<8k token prompt repeated>","stream":true,"max_tokens":4096}'
maria_g: repro confirmed. With that prompt we see the worker memory climb and then a crash. Logs from host show repeated: "cuda: out of memory (OOM)" then segfault. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T09:13:02Z] runner: Allocation failed: CUDA OOM while reserving 2.3GB
[2026-03-18T09:13:02Z] runner: kernel panic: invalid read at 0x7fffa3... (segfault)
[2026-03-18T09:13:02Z] docker: container exited with status 139
```
alex_w: stack traces point to KV cache growth -- NV memory not reclaimed fast enough. Any prefetch changes in this deploy? Maria: we changed prefetch heuristic to be more aggressive for v2-quant (PR #4123) to reduce cold-start latency.
karen_p: Customer is on a paid SLA. Support message queued but they want ETA and workaround. Please provide hotfix options.
support_andy: Drafting message: "We're seeing upstream worker crashes when long streaming requests hit v2-quant. We're actively mitigating and will provide ETA. For now, please avoid extremely long single-stream prompts; we'll follow up with a rolling fix." Approve?
alex_w: immediate mitigations I propose:
 - route traffic for ACME to v2-256 (non-quant) or a dedicated pool
 - rollback prefetch heuristic for v2-quant (revert PR #4123)
 - add per-session token limit for hosted streaming temporarily
jamal: quick command to pin model for a tenant:
```
POST /v1/admin/tenants/acme/policy
{ "route_model": "redwood/v2-256@2026-03-10" }
```
maria_g: I can prepare a rollback patch to revert the prefetch change and a small patch that enforces KV cap in the runtime: `MAX_KV_TOKENS=4096` env var. Rolling revert ready in ~20m.
eng-runtime-bot: Related logs uploaded: https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/6135791357?span=09:10-09:20
alex_w: short-term action owner assignments:
 - pin ACME to v2-256: jamal
 - revert prefetch + deploy KV cap: maria_g
 - customer comms: karen_p and support_andy
jamal: pinning now, will confirm when traffic shifts
karen_p: I'll send the customer a note: "We've temporarily routed your long-stream requests to a stable non-quant model and are investigating root cause. Expect reduced latency within 5-10m."
support_andy: sent to ACME, included suggested mitigation and workaround.
maria_g: deploying rollback to canary now (canary pool size 2): `kubectl set image deploy/runner v2-quant=runner:v2026-03-18-revert` — monitoring.
alex_w: while deploy rolls, enable extra logging and eviction for KV cache on canaries: `export MAX_KV_TOKENS=4096` and `KV_EVICT=true` for the pod template.
eng-runtime-bot: canary pod logs: still seeing memory climb but no segfault yet (10s window). Will continue to watch p95.
jamal: ACME traffic showing fewer 503s after routing, p95 dropped ~60% per dashboard.
karen_p: Customer acknowledged and is OK with temporary routing. They asked if this will affect fine-tuning quality — said it's okay for now.
alex_w: postmortem action items (initial):
 - revert prefetch heuristic permanently until we have memory bounds tests (maria_g)
 - add per-model KV memory accounting and hard caps (eng-runtime)
 - add tests that simulate 20k token streaming to catch OOM during CI (sre/qa)
 - investigate quantized model kernel causing segfault (research)
jamal: FYI repro command used for devs:
```
node tools/repro-stream.js --model redwood/v2-quant@latest --context 18000 --stream
```
maria_g: deploy successful to canary, rolling to prod after 15m a/b observe window. No further segfaults on canary.
oncall-bot: incident update: mitigation applied, routing and rollback in progress, customer partially mitigated. Continuing monitoring.
support_andy: closing loop with customer and asking for confirmation; will reopen if they see regression.
karen_p: thanks all. If anyone sees new 139 exits tag me. I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem doc.
alex_w: thanks team — tracking as Sev2 for follow-up.
